# thermify

**Efficient, reproducible and spatially explicit agroclimatic thermal
indices in R.**

`thermify` computes heat and chill accumulation indices from daily or
hourly temperatures, and from monthly climatologies such as WorldClim
after a mean-preserving temporal densification.

| Family | Methods |
|----|----|
| Growing degree-days | average, single sine, single triangle, double sine, double triangle; horizontal, vertical and intermediate upper cutoffs; degree-hours |
| Chilling hours | analytical sine and triangle estimates from daily extremes; counts on hourly data |
| Chill units | Utah model (Richardson et al. 1974) |
| Chill portions | Dynamic model (Fishman et al. 1987; Erez et al. 1990), resumable across blocks |
| Temporal reconstruction | monthly to daily (`pchip_mp`, natively or via [tempify](https://github.com/djwillichile/tempify)); daily to hourly (sine or Linvill) |
| Spatial | block-wise processing of [`terra::SpatRaster`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/SpatRaster-class.html) stacks, GeoTIFF and NetCDF output; regional WorldClim 2.1 reads; official DPA 2023 boundaries of Cauquenes ([`cauquenes_boundary()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/cauquenes_boundary.md)) |

> \[!IMPORTANT\] Monthly climate normals are not daily or hourly
> observations. Indices reconstructed from monthly climatologies are
> model-based estimates and must be validated against observations
> before decision-critical use.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("djwillichile/thermify@v0.3.0")   # release
remotes::install_github("djwillichile/thermify")          # development
```

[`library(thermify)`](https://github.com/djwillichile/thermify) also
attaches `terra`, so
[`rast()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/rast.html),
[`vect()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/vect.html),
[`plot()`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/reference/plot.html) and the
other `terra` functions are available directly. The optional
[tempify](https://github.com/djwillichile/tempify) backend is set up
automatically in interactive sessions when `reticulate` (\>= 1.41) is
installed: the first use builds and caches a Python environment with it
(see
[`install_tempify()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/install_tempify.md)
for a persistent environment). Without it, `thermify` uses an equivalent
native R engine.

## Quick start

``` r

library(thermify)

tmin <- c(4, 8, 12, 15)
tmax <- c(16, 22, 28, 34)

# Growing degree-days (degC day)
degree_days(tmin, tmax, method = "single_sine", base = 10)
degree_days(tmin, tmax, method = "single_sine", base = 10, upper = 30,
            cutoff = "vertical")

# Chilling hours estimated from daily extremes (h)
chill_hours(c(-2, 4), c(10, 12), method = "sine")

# Hourly series (observed or reconstructed)
hourly <- hourly_temperatures(rep(3, 30), rep(13, 30), latitude = -35.97,
                              doy = 152:181)
chill_units(hourly, method = "utah", output = "total")
chill_portions(hourly, method = "dynamic", output = "total")
```

From monthly climatology to seasonal indices for one location:

``` r

tmin <- c(11.4, 11.1, 9.2, 6.8, 5.3, 3.9, 3.1, 3.6, 4.6, 6.3, 8.4, 10.3)
tmax <- c(29.6, 29.2, 26.5, 21.9, 17.2, 13.9, 13.6, 15.3, 17.9, 21.2,
          24.9, 28.2)
res <- thermify(tmin, tmax, input = "monthly", latitude = -35.97,
                temporal = "auto", interpolation = "pchip_mp",
                indices = c("gdd", "ch", "cu", "cp"))
res$summary
```

WorldClim 2.1 at 30 arc-seconds can be read for a region only,
transferring just the bytes of that window (optionally masked by a
polygon):

``` r

win  <- study_window(lon = -72.3225, lat = -35.9671, size_km = 20)
tmin <- worldclim_region("tmin", win, path = "data")
tmax <- worldclim_region("tmax", win, path = "data")

# Official DPA 2023 boundary of the Cauquenes commune, as a mask
comuna <- cauquenes_boundary("comuna")        # or "provincia"
tmin_c <- worldclim_region("tmin", comuna, path = "data", mask = TRUE)
```

When does a crop reach its degree-day requirement, or a cultivar its
chill requirement?

``` r

# station: data frame with daily date, tmin, tmax from 1 Sep to 30 Apr
gdd <- degree_days(station$tmin, station$tmax, method = "single_sine",
                   base = 10)
threshold_date(gdd, station$date, threshold = 500)
```

For rasters,
[`thermify_rast()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/thermify_rast.md)
applies the same workflow block by block to 12-layer `SpatRaster` stacks
and writes one file per index, reporting progress (blocks done, elapsed
time and estimated time remaining).

## Verification

- Unit tests cover every method against closed forms, numerical
  integration, an independent transcription of the Dynamic model
  equations, block equivalence and raster geometry.

- `inst/verification/verify_references.R` cross-checks thermify against
  `chillR` (Dynamic, Utah, chilling hours, day length, Linvill hours)
  and `degday` (UC IPM degree-day formulas). Current differences are
  below 1e-12, except for one documented convention in the pre-dawn
  Linvill curve (`night = "chillr"` reproduces chillR exactly).

- The native `pchip_mp` engine reproduces tempify to within 1e-13 degC.

- About 400 expectations in unit, acceptance (one per [user
  story](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/docs/USER_STORIES.md)),
  integration and error-path tests, with 94 % line coverage; see
  [docs/TESTING.md](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/docs/TESTING.md).

Computational verification is not empirical validation; see
[`vignette("validation")`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/articles/validation.md)
for the station-based protocol.

## Case study

[`examples/cauquenes`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/examples/cauquenes)
computes all indices for a 20 x 20 km window around Cauquenes (Maule,
Chile) from WorldClim 2.1.

## Documentation

Site: <https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/>. Articles cover GDD
methods, chill models, the tempify integration, the Cauquenes tutorial
and the validation protocol.

# Package index

## Growing degree-days

- [`degree_days()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/degree_days.md)
  : Growing degree-days from daily minimum and maximum temperatures
- [`degree_hours()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/degree_hours.md)
  : Degree-hours from hourly temperatures

## Chill models

- [`chill_hours()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/chill_hours.md)
  : Chilling hours estimated from daily minimum and maximum temperatures
- [`chill_hours_hourly()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/chill_hours_hourly.md)
  : Chilling hours counted from hourly temperatures
- [`chill_units()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/chill_units.md)
  : Utah model chill units
- [`utah_weights()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/utah_weights.md)
  : Utah model hourly weights
- [`chill_portions()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/chill_portions.md)
  : Dynamic model chill portions

## Temporal reconstruction

- [`densify_monthly()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/densify_monthly.md)
  : Densify monthly climatologies to daily values
- [`densify_diagnostics()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/densify_diagnostics.md)
  : Diagnostics of a monthly-to-daily densification
- [`tempify_available()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/tempify_available.md)
  : Is the tempify Python package available?
- [`install_tempify()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/install_tempify.md)
  : Install the tempify Python backend
- [`tempify_version()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/tempify_version.md)
  : Version information of the tempify backend
- [`hourly_temperatures()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/hourly_temperatures.md)
  : Reconstruct hourly temperatures from daily extremes
- [`daylength()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/daylength.md)
  : Astronomical day length, sunrise and sunset

## Workflows and periods

- [`thermify()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/thermify.md)
  : Compute several thermal indices for one location
- [`thermify_rast()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/thermify_rast.md)
  : Thermal indices from monthly climatology rasters
- [`plot(`*`<thermify_rast>`*`)`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/plot.thermify_rast.md)
  [`print(`*`<thermify_rast>`*`)`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/plot.thermify_rast.md)
  : Plot and print the maps produced by thermify_rast()
- [`season_days()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/season_days.md)
  : Select the days of an accumulation period
- [`threshold_date()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/threshold_date.md)
  : Date on which an accumulated index reaches a threshold

## Validation

- [`prepare_station_hourly()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/prepare_station_hourly.md)
  : Prepare an hourly station record for validation
- [`validate_station()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/validate_station.md)
  : Validate thermal-index estimates against an hourly station record
- [`validation_metrics()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/validation_metrics.md)
  : Agreement metrics between estimated and observed values

## Spatial data

- [`study_window()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/study_window.md)
  : Square study window around a point
- [`worldclim_region()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/worldclim_region.md)
  : Read WorldClim 2.1 at 30 arc-seconds for a region only
- [`worldclim_monthly()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/worldclim_monthly.md)
  : Download (or reuse) WorldClim 2.1 monthly temperature normals
- [`check_monthly_climate()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/check_monthly_climate.md)
  : Validate a pair of monthly temperature rasters
- [`cauquenes`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/cauquenes.md)
  : Administrative boundaries of Cauquenes (DPA 2023)
- [`cauquenes_boundary()`](https://djwillichile.github.io/thermify/reference/cauquenes_boundary.md)
  : Cauquenes boundary at a given administrative level
